title: How to Prepare a Landing Page Project Before Hiring
h1: How to prepare a landing page project before hiring
description: Prepare a landing page project: single goal, audience, offer, page structure, proof, content, tracking and what to ask a designer or developer.
intro: A landing page is a single page built to get one action: a purchase, a sign-up, a booking request or a download. It is often the page people reach after clicking an ad or a link. Because it has one job, small decisions about wording, layout and trust make a large difference. This article explains how to prepare before hiring a designer or developer so the page can work from the first day.

faq.q: What makes a landing page different from a normal page?
faq.a: It has one goal and removes distractions such as extra menus and unrelated links.
Ideally someone who understands your customers. Ask whether the designer writes copy or whether you or a copywriter will provide it.

faq.q: Do I need to build several versions?
faq.a: Often one page per audience or campaign works best, because the message matches what people clicked.

faq.q: How do I know it works?
faq.a: Track the main action and compare the share of visitors who complete it over a fair period.

faq.q: Which platform should it be on?
faq.a: Use a platform your team can edit, or ask the freelancer to recommend one and explain the ongoing costs.
